article.summary: ActiveMemory/ctx is a file based context system for coding assistants. Its Go CLI manages project-local .context/ Markdown files for tasks, decisions, learnings, conventions, session journals, and knowledge workflows. This is a selected source review, not a runtime or benchmark result.

who_what.text: The target is the explicitly listed ActiveMemory/ctx repository, a public file based Go project whose README describes context persistence for coding assistants and publishes an Apache-2.0 license. No contact email was found in the checked README.
The separate diegoxtr/ctx-open repository has a different README and implementation. The listed ActiveMemory URL did not redirect there; the earlier article had conflated the two catalog records.

architecture.text: The README and CLI reference describe project-local .context/ Markdown files as the storage surface. Task, decision, learning and convention commands map to TASKS.md, DECISIONS.md, LEARNINGS.md and CONVENTIONS.md; commands resolve the project from the current working directory and require Git.

The journal command imports supported assistant transcripts into editable files under .context/journal/. The reference documents incremental import, growth detection, preservation of edited entries, and optional entry locks.

behavior.text: Write: typed CLI commands add tasks, decisions, learnings and conventions to named Markdown files. The reference documents provenance fields including session ID, branch and commit, plus structured decision and learning fields.

Update and cleanup: the reference documents task completion, archive and snapshot operations, formatting, sync and drift checks. Journal import checks for edits before rewriting grown transcripts and supports locks. The inspected references do not establish a general deletion API or that every edit retains prior values.

Retrieval: the README demonstrates ctx agent --budget to produce an AI-ready context packet. Journal commands list, filter, and show session records. Retrieval ranking and recall quality were not established by these selected sources.

Scope and provenance: documented CLI context is rooted at the current project and its .context directory; context entries can record session ID, branch and commit. The selected dream code has a path write guard for dreams/ and ideas/, with a promotion exception for specs/. This does not prove read isolation, general authorization, or runtime enforcement across every write path.

Evidence and efficiency: structured fields and imported transcripts can retain source context, and the CLI offers a context packet budget. These mechanisms do not validate the truth of stored claims. No latency, token, cost, or storage measurement was collected.

metrics.evidence: Context packet and journal retrieval commands are documented; no retrieval or abstention probes were run.
Edit, sync, drift, and journal protection behavior are documented; no correction workload was run.
The inspected references describe archival and snapshots but do not establish general deletion behavior; no deletion workload was run.
The README describes a current-project .context boundary and selected dream code has write guards; no cross-project probe was run.
Entries can carry provenance metadata; no claim-to-source adjudication was run.
No timed retrieval workload or latency distribution was collected.
Writes and context packet generation are documented; searchable-after-write timing was not measured.
The CLI exposes a context budget; no token or provider-cost results were collected.
Markdown file storage is documented; no bytes-per-item or storage footprint measurement was made.

limits.text: This record is based on selected pinned documentation and one code file. It does not establish behavior across the full codebase, runtime correctness, or robustness under concurrency and failure.
The reviewed README documents local project files and current-directory scoping. The review did not establish a multi-user authorization boundary or read isolation.
No ctx workload, tests or benchmarks were executed. All metric domains remain unmeasured.
